correctness.rationale: Conditional sampling gives the exact four-monomial matrix \(B_{n,s}\); its weighted polynomial identity is \(\mathbb E[V_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]-V_k=sP_n(s)x_k^2\). The leading and variance coefficients are positive and the \((x,m)\) determinant factor is strictly positive for every \(n\ge2,s>0\). For \(P_n(s)<0\) telescoping gives summability of expected iterate squares, while an exact table-norm recurrence forces stored gradients to zero. At and above the unique positive zero, expected positive energy cannot tend to zero from any nonzero scalar state; positive eigenvector localization proves necessity in arbitrary SPD dimensions. Formal SymPy polynomial checks and 270 independently enumerated exact-rational conditional expectation cases executed successfully. The code supports, but does not replace, the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2014 source defines original SAGA and proves conservative general sufficient rates, not an all-initialization necessary-and-sufficient condition. The 2019 ``optimal stepsize`` theorem concerns optimized guaranteed smoothness bounds and does not imply the exact stability frontier on an identical-Hessian family. The known \(n=2\) cutoff is a covered special case; the all-\(n\) threshold, its sharp failure from any nonzero scalar state, strict sample-count law, and arbitrary SPD extension are not consequences of that special case. The related stochastic finite-sum and spectral-method search hits do not cover the same SAGA hypotheses and conclusion. An equivalent unnamed older stochastic linear-systems result remains a real residual risk, so originality is qualified rather than purported certified exhaustively.
residual_risks: An older stochastic linear-systems or incremental-memory convergence theorem may imply the exact all-\(n\) scalar threshold under a different name.
The first SAGA arXiv paper has no printed MSC; primary 65K05 ownership is independently supported by the later SAGA-containing numerical-optimization survey.
Semantic searches and inspected source sections are not an exhaustive proof of novel priority.

value.rationale: The original SAGA algorithm has a practically motivated gradient-memory step-size question: even when every component gradient is identical at the same evaluation point, saved values from different times can destabilize the iteration. The theorem gives a sharp all-sample-count and all-SPD convergence classification, exact energy certificate, first-order sample-count sensitivity and threshold asymptotics. It resolves a natural benchmark completely, provides a direct counterexample to transferring the full-gradient ceiling, and goes beyond routine numerical substitution into the previously known two-component boundary.
